Yes. If possible, even a coloured copy, because there are different colours on the...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll then deal with the other documents. Could you please guide us, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2506B, specialist's report, diagnosis, from Dobrinja Hospital. P2506B.1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we first stop here. Mr. Stamp, the document is not fully translated, especially the stamp is not translated, and it seems that might be a relevant part of the document. I think the Chamber would, as usual, require the Prosecution to give a full translation, especially here where the stamp is considered as of importance by the Defence. So perhaps we could do it that we admitted the document in evidence provisionally under the condition that, on short notice, a full translation will be provided. And if the translation is provided and if there are any questions to it, of course the Defence will have an opportunity to make whatever observations in that respect before we finally admit it into evidence. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, we have some other documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D86, document bearing ERN number 0038-0015, list of names. D87, document bearing two ERN numbers, the first being 0038-0026; the second, 0026-7853. D88, document bearing ERN number 0215-6335. Exhibit D89, document bearing ERN number 0215-5961. Exhibit D90, document bearing ERN number 0215-6203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There are no objections. We have had a short explanation of what the relevance of these documents would be. I noticed that the only testimony about these documents is that the witness read parts of the documents, which, of course, is not necessary, I would say. You could call any witness and ask him whether he could read what is on a document. I would rather prefer that if these documents are considered to be relevant for the case of one of the parties, I assume that it's relevant for the case of the Defence, that then the parties agree upon whether line 7 contains certain words or not. It's really a waste of time to ask -- you could have asked any journalist or military expert to do the same. And I even may reveal to you that this Chamber is to some extent able of reading it, so I would like to invite the parties to solve these problems out of Court. Of course, there should be a way of introducing relevant documents to the Court but it's not necessary to read specific lines and then say thank you for reading it to us. Then this ends the Court session of today. Are there any additional observations to be made at this moment? Perhaps, in view of next week? If so -- if there's any observation to be made at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may through the Court indicate that the witness Edin Suljic, who is the next witness to be called -- there were, I think, four documents listed to be adduced through him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see five on the list. But I don't know whether it's the last list or not. I get sometimes a bit -- I have 2286, 2365, 2366, 3061, and 2264. And that's the list of 2nd of April. But perhaps I disregarded the... I've got the 4th of April. The next list, there are only three. The list of the 4th of April indicates three numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is it the position of the Court that it refers to three documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the former one, the list of the 2nd of April, showed five, and the list of the 4th of April shows three, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I wasn't aware that the Court assistant had been -- I was not aware of the level of efficiency. Of course, I was aware that she had been efficient. I have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have absolutely nothing to add to that, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then, I wish everyone a good weekend. I especially thank the interpreters and those who are technically assisting us for enabling us to finalise for this week, which took some extra time. We'll adjourn, and we'll adjourn until next Monday at 9.00 in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.56 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of April, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
